findings.title: POST /auth/logout accepts request with no Authorization header
findings.description: The endpoint POST /auth/logout returned HTTP 200 when called with no Authorization header. Authentication should be enforced and unauthenticated or invalidly authenticated requests should be rejected.
findings.expected: HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 403 Forbidden
findings.suggested_fix: Return HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate header when credentials are missing or invalid.

findings.title: IDOR: carol can edit bob's post
findings.description: Carol sent PATCH /posts/521, which is owned by bob, and received HTTP 200. The server should verify the authenticated user owns the post before allowing edits.
findings.reproduction: curl -X PATCH https://backend-agent-test.onrender.com/posts/521 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <carol_token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"body": "Overwritten by carol"}'
findings.expected: HTTP 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found
findings.suggested_fix: Check post.author_id == current_user.id before allowing PATCH.

findings.title: Input not rejected: Age field accepts string value

findings.expected: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity
findings.suggested_fix: Add a non-negative integer constraint to the age field in the update schema and avoid unsafe type coercion.

findings.title: Input not rejected: Age field accepts negative integer

findings.suggested_fix: Add a non-negative integer constraint to the age field in the update schema and avoid unsafe type coercion.

findings.title: Input not rejected: Age field accepts float value

findings.expected: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity
findings.suggested_fix: Add a non-negative integer constraint to the age field in the update schema and avoid unsafe type coercion.

findings.title: Input not rejected: Negative limit accepted without validation error
findings.description: GET /posts with limit=-1 returned HTTP 500. Invalid pagination values should be rejected.
findings.expected: HTTP 422 or clamped to 0 — negative limit is nonsensical
findings.suggested_fix: Add ge=0 constraints to limit and offset parameters.

findings.title: Input not rejected: Negative offset accepted without validation error
findings.description: GET /posts with offset=-1 returned HTTP 200. Invalid pagination values should be rejected.
findings.expected: HTTP 422 or clamped to 0 — negative offset is nonsensical
findings.suggested_fix: Add ge=0 constraints to limit and offset parameters.

findings.title: Uncapped pagination: limit=999999 returns oversized payload
findings.description: GET /posts?limit=999999 returned HTTP 200 with a 980,329-byte response body. There is no upper bound enforced on the limit parameter.

findings.expected: HTTP 422 or response capped at a maximum page size
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce a maximum value, such as le=100, on the limit parameter.

findings.title: Input not rejected: Post created with empty body string
findings.description: POST /posts with empty body string returned HTTP 201. A post with no meaningful content should be rejected.
findings.expected: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity
findings.suggested_fix: Add minLength: 1 constraint to the post body field in the request schema.

findings.title: Business logic flaw: user can follow themselves
findings.description: POST /users/3/follow with carol's own token returned HTTP 200. A user following themselves creates an invalid social graph state.
findings.expected: HTTP 400 or 422 — cannot follow yourself
findings.suggested_fix: Check that follower_id != followee_id before inserting the follow relationship. Return HTTP 400 with a clear message.

findings.title: Unlike a never-liked post returns success silently
findings.description: DELETE /posts/521/like as carol returned HTTP 200. If no like existed, this should be documented as idempotent or return 404.
findings.expected: HTTP 404 Not Found or documented idempotent success
findings.suggested_fix: Return 404 when the like relationship does not exist, or document idempotency.

findings.title: Double-delete post returns success on already-deleted resource
findings.description: Deleting post 524 twice returned HTTP 200 on the second attempt. The post no longer exists, so the API should return 404 or explicitly document idempotent delete behavior.
findings.expected: HTTP 404 Not Found on second delete or documented idempotent success
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the post exists before deleting and return 404 if absent.

findings.title: Ghost resource returns unexpected status: Like a nonexistent post
findings.description: POST /posts/999999999/like returned HTTP 200 for a nonexistent resource ID (999999999). Expected HTTP 404 Not Found, 403 Forbidden, or 422 validation failure.
findings.expected: HTTP 404 Not Found
findings.suggested_fix: Return 404 for all references to nonexistent resource IDs.

findings.title: Login with missing password returns HTTP 401, expected 422
findings.description: POST /auth/login with only username and no password returned HTTP 401. Missing required fields should return 400 Bad Request or 422 Unprocessable Entity.
findings.expected: HTTP 400 Bad Request or 422 Unprocessable Entity
findings.suggested_fix: Validate required fields username and password and return 400/422 when either field is missing.

findings.title: Malformed JSON body leaks internals on POST /auth/login
findings.description: POST /auth/login with malformed JSON body returned HTTP 500. Traceback signals found: ['Internal Server Error'].
findings.expected: HTTP 400 or 422 with a clean JSON error message
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap JSON parse errors in a global exception handler that returns a clean 400/422 response without leaking internals.

findings.title: Malformed JSON body leaks internals on POST /posts
findings.description: POST /posts with malformed JSON body returned HTTP 500. Traceback signals found: ['Internal Server Error'].
findings.reproduction: curl -X POST https://backend-agent-test.onrender.com/posts -H 'Authorization: Bearer <bob_token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{not valid json!!!'
findings.expected: HTTP 400 or 422 with a clean JSON error message
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap JSON parse errors in a global exception handler that returns a clean 400/422 response without leaking internals.

findings.title: Wrong Content-Type causes server error on POST /posts
findings.description: POST /posts with Content-Type: text/plain returned HTTP 500. Leak signals: ['Internal Server Error'].
findings.expected: HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type or HTTP 422
findings.suggested_fix: Return 415 for unsupported Content-Type headers.

findings.title: Missing security header: X-Content-Type-Options
findings.description: The response does not include the X-Content-Type-Options header. Without this header, browsers may MIME-sniff responses.
findings.expected: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' to all responses.

findings.title: Missing security header: X-Frame-Options
findings.description: The response does not include the X-Frame-Options header. This can allow the API to be embedded in iframes.
findings.expected: X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or SAMEORIGIN to all responses.

findings.title: Missing security header: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)
findings.description: The API does not send a Strict-Transport-Security header. As this is an HTTPS API, HSTS should be enforced to prevent protocol downgrade attacks.
findings.expected: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
findings.suggested_fix: Add HSTS header with a max-age of at least 1 year.

findings.title: CORS: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is wildcard (*)
findings.description: The API responds to cross-origin requests with 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *', allowing any origin to make browser-based requests.
findings.expected: Specific allowed origin or no ACAO header
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict CORS to a whitelist of known trusted origins.

findings.title: CORS: Wildcard origin combined with Allow-Credentials: true
findings.description: The API sets both 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' and 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. This indicates a misconfigured CORS policy.
findings.expected: Credentials only allowed for specific trusted origins
findings.suggested_fix: Never combine wildcard origin with Allow-Credentials: true. Use an explicit origin whitelist.

findings.title: No rate limiting on POST /auth/login (15 requests, no 429)
findings.description: Fired 15 consecutive failed login attempts against POST /auth/login. All returned authentication failures without any HTTP 429 throttling response.
findings.reproduction:
for i in $(seq 1 15); do
  curl -X POST https://backend-agent-test.onrender.com/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username": "alice", "password": "WRONG"}'
done
findings.expected: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests after repeated failures
findings.actual: All 15 requests returned auth failures with no throttling. Status code distribution: {401: 15}
findings.suggested_fix: Implement IP-based and username-based throttling on /auth/login, for example max 5 failures per minute with progressive delay.

findings.title: No rate limiting on POST /auth/register (15 requests, no 429)
findings.description: Fired 15 registration requests against POST /auth/register. 15 succeeded with no throttling or 429 response.
findings.reproduction:
for i in $(seq 1 15); do
  curl -X POST https://backend-agent-test.onrender.com/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username": "spam_$i", "password": "pass", "email": "spam_$i@x.com"}'
done
findings.expected: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests after repeated registration attempts
findings.suggested_fix: Apply IP-based rate limiting to POST /auth/register, for example max 3 registrations per IP per hour.

findings.expected: HTTP 200 or 204 with Allow header

findings.title: OPTIONS /auth/login returned 405, expected 200/204

findings.expected: HTTP 400 or 422
findings.suggested_fix: Handle empty bodies with a 400 or 422 response.

findings.title: Trailing slash inconsistency: /posts vs /posts/ return different status codes
findings.description: GET /posts returned HTTP 200, while GET /posts/ returned HTTP 307. Trailing slash handling should be consistent.
findings.expected: Same status as /posts: HTTP 200
findings.suggested_fix: Configure consistent trailing-slash handling at the router level.

findings.title: Inconsistent post shape between feed and single-post endpoints
findings.description: GET /posts and GET /posts/{id} return different field sets for post objects. Only in feed: ['author']. Only in single: ['authorName'].
findings.expected: Same post object shape on both endpoints
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same post serializer for both feed and single-post endpoints.

findings.title: Uncapped pagination: limit=10000 returns 980,460 bytes
findings.description: GET /posts?limit=10000 returned 458 items in 980,460 bytes (957.5 KB) in 260ms. There is no server-enforced maximum on the limit parameter.

findings.title: Missing Cache-Control header on GET /posts
findings.description: GET /posts does not include a Cache-Control header. Without caching directives, clients and proxies cannot cache responses.
findings.expected: Cache-Control header present
findings.suggested_fix: Add Cache-Control headers to public read endpoints. For frequently changing feeds, use a short max-age.

findings.title: Missing ETag and Last-Modified on GET /posts
findings.description: GET /posts provides no ETag or Last-Modified header. These headers enable conditional requests and reduce bandwidth.
findings.expected: ETag or Last-Modified header present
findings.suggested_fix: Add ETag headers or Last-Modified timestamps to public read endpoints.

findings.title: Missing Cache-Control header on GET /posts/{post_id}
findings.description: GET /posts/521 does not include a Cache-Control header. Without caching directives, clients and proxies cannot cache responses.
findings.expected: Cache-Control header present
findings.suggested_fix: Add Cache-Control headers to public read endpoints. For frequently changing feeds, use a short max-age.

findings.title: Missing ETag and Last-Modified on GET /posts/{post_id}
findings.description: GET /posts/521 provides no ETag or Last-Modified header. These headers enable conditional requests and reduce bandwidth.
findings.expected: ETag or Last-Modified header present
findings.suggested_fix: Add ETag headers or Last-Modified timestamps to public read endpoints.

findings.title: Spec drift: Authorization header marked required:false but endpoint enforces auth
findings.description: The OpenAPI spec marks the Authorization header as 'required: false' on GET /users/me and other protected endpoints. However, calling the endpoint without a token returns HTTP 401, proving auth is required.
findings.expected: Spec should declare Authorization as required:true or use a required bearer security scheme
findings.actual: Spec says required:false, but API returns HTTP 401 without auth
findings.suggested_fix: Use OpenAPI security schemes such as BearerAuth instead of manually declaring the Authorization header as an optional parameter.

findings.title: Spec drift: POST /auth/logout returns fields but spec documents empty response {}
findings.description: POST /auth/logout returned HTTP 200 with body {'detail': 'logged out'}. The spec defines the response schema as empty {}.
findings.expected: Empty JSON body {} as per spec
findings.suggested_fix: Update the spec to document the actual logout response schema.

findings.title: Documented endpoint returns 5xx: GET /users/me
findings.description: GET /users/me returned HTTP 500. A documented endpoint should not return 5xx for a valid request.
findings.expected: HTTP 200/201/204 or a documented 4xx client error
findings.suggested_fix: Investigate and handle the server error on this route.
